purpose: Separates three questions that were coupled for /acquire/: ACCESS (can a visitor open the URL: yes, it is served), PUBLICATION (is a release authorized: release ledger / Contract C / R11) and INDEXING (may search engines index it). An entry here is a per-URL indexing CEILING: the authority serves 'noindex, follow' and keeps the URL out of every sitemap, whatever the release ledger, a URL decision, Contract C or an R11 certification would otherwise allow. A ceiling can only lower a directive; it never makes any page indexable and never changes access or the canonical.
rules: Only page_class 'commercial_access' is accepted. A scientific or conceptual reference never carries a ceiling.
A ceiling is refused (ignored and reported) for any URL bound to a Knowledge Object render spec: references keep their own Contract C rules.
Do not implement a ceiling with robots.txt: crawlers must be able to fetch the page to see its noindex.
Changing or removing a ceiling is an explicit owner policy decision recorded here; no ledger change, URL decision or release removes it.

policies.access: public by direct URL (HTTP 200, linked from site navigation)
policies.duration: indefinite, until the owner explicitly changes this policy
policies.rationale: /acquire/ is a buyer-oriented commercial access page, not a scientific, conceptual or general reference page. It is reachable by prospective buyers through its direct URL and is not meant to compete for organic search visibility with BISULFID's reference content.

provenance.channel: owner instruction in the Claude Code review session (Release-01, 'Permanent Buyer-Access Policy for /acquire/'), 2026-10-30
provenance.note: This records the owner's policy decision as given in conversation. It is not a signed repository approval: no approved_by identity or approval timestamp is entered. Because a ceiling can only make a page LESS visible, the authority applies it from this record; the formal sign-off of the PR-B page change remains URL-DEC-R03-ACQUIRE-001.
